title: Admin JWT bypass via jwt.decode() without signature verification
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/auth/auth.controller.js:287`
**Root Cause:** The `POST /api/auth/admin/authorize` endpoint calls `jwt.decode(token)` which performs only base64 decoding with zero cryptographic verification. Any crafted JWT payload passes the admin authorization check because the signature is never validated against the Keycloak JWKS keys. The existing `verifyKeycloakToken()` function performs proper RS256 JWKS verification but is not called here.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
In `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/auth/auth.controller.js` at line 287, replace `jwt.decode(token)` with `await verifyKeycloakToken(token)`. Ensure the function is already imported (it is used elsewhere in the file). Wrap in try/catch: if verification fails throw a 401 error. Never use `jwt.decode()` for any authorization decision.
fixEvidence: CWE-347 / OWASP A02 — auth.controller.js:287 — jwt.decode() used for admin authorization; attacker can forge any JWT payload

title: OAuth callback uses unverified jwt.decode() to link user accounts
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/auth/auth.controller.js:66`
**Root Cause:** The `decodePayload()` helper function uses `jwt.decode()` on the Keycloak access token obtained from the token exchange. The `sub`, `email`, and `organizationId` claims extracted from this unverified token are used to look up and link MongoDB user records. An attacker who can intercept or substitute the token response can supply arbitrary claims and hijack any user account.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
In `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/auth/auth.controller.js` at the `decodePayload()` function (line 66), replace `jwt.decode(accessToken)` with `const payload = await verifyKeycloakToken(accessToken)`. Remove the `decodePayload` wrapper function and call `verifyKeycloakToken` directly in `handleOAuthCallback`. Ensure the return value is treated as the verified payload.
fixEvidence: CWE-347 / OWASP A02 — auth.controller.js:66 — decodePayload() uses jwt.decode(); crafted token can hijack existing account

title: DEV MODE base64 JWT decode with zero signature verification in assistant-service
description:
**Files:** `assistant-service/src/plugins/keycloak.ts:135-155`
**Root Cause:** When `NODE_ENV === 'development'` and a Bearer token is present, the code performs `JSON.parse(Buffer.from(parts[1], 'base64'))` — a raw base64 decode with no cryptographic signature verification. This means an attacker who constructs any valid-looking JWT header and payload (but with a fake or empty signature) can authenticate as any user they choose, with any role or organization claim.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
Delete the entire DEV MODE branch in `assistant-service/src/plugins/keycloak.ts` lines 135-155 that performs the base64 decode. The production `jwtVerify()` path (using the Keycloak JWKS endpoint) must be the only code path for token validation. If local development requires authentication, run a local Keycloak instance or use the real staging Keycloak with test credentials.
fixEvidence: CWE-347 / OWASP A02 — assistant-service/keycloak.ts:140 — attacker controls token content; impersonate any user

title: DEV MODE no-auth fallback injects hardcoded admin for all unauthenticated requests
description:
**Files:** `assistant-service/src/plugins/keycloak.ts:158-175`
**Root Cause:** When `NODE_ENV === 'development'` and no `Authorization` header is present, the code populates `request.user` with a hardcoded object containing an admin organization ID and user ID. This makes every assistant-service endpoint publicly accessible without any credentials, with full admin context. Any unauthenticated HTTP request to any assistant endpoint in a non-production deployment gains admin-level access.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
Delete the no-auth fallback block in `assistant-service/src/plugins/keycloak.ts` (approximately lines 158-175) that sets `request.user` to a hardcoded object when no Authorization header is present. Replace with: `return reply.status(401).send({ error: 'Unauthorized', message: 'No authentication token provided' })`. There must be no fallback authentication path.
fixEvidence: CWE-287 / OWASP A01 — assistant-service/keycloak.ts:162 — all assistant endpoints publicly accessible with full admin rights

title: Document upload endpoint authentication explicitly disabled
description:
**Files:** `python-notebookAI-service/routers/documents.py:89-101`
**Root Cause:** The `POST /api/v1/documents/upload` endpoint has its `Depends(verify_token)` dependency commented out and replaced with a hardcoded `user_info = {'user_id': 'test_user', 'organizationId': None}`. Any unauthenticated caller can upload arbitrary files to S3 and trigger AI processing pipelines, incurring cost, storage usage, and potentially poisoning the vector store with malicious content.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
In `python-notebookAI-service/routers/documents.py`, at the upload endpoint (lines 89-101), uncomment `user_info: Dict = Depends(verify_token)` as a function parameter and remove the mock `user_info` assignment block. Add `organizationId: user_info.get('organizationId')` to all S3 and database operations to enforce tenant scoping.
fixEvidence: CWE-287 / OWASP A01 — python-notebookAI-service/routers/documents.py:89-101 — auth commented out; mock user injected

title: All ai_policy_generator_python routes publicly accessible — zero authentication
description:
**Files:** `ai_policy_generator_python/app/api/routes/policy_generation.py:71`, `ai_policy_generator_python/app/api/routes/rag_pipeline.py`, `ai_policy_generator_python/app/api/routes/analytics.py:63`
**Root Cause:** None of the route handlers in the policy generator service have authentication dependencies. The service has no `auth.py` module. All endpoints including `POST /api/v1/policy/generate`, all RAG pipeline endpoints, and all analytics endpoints are publicly accessible — exposing LLM cost, MongoDB data, and generation analytics to any unauthenticated caller.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
Create `ai_policy_generator_python/app/auth.py` modelled on `python-notebookAI-service/auth.py`. Implement `verify_token(credentials: HTTPAuthorizationCredentials = Depends(security))` using the Keycloak JWKS endpoint. In `policy_generation.py`, `rag_pipeline.py`, and `analytics.py`, add `user_info: Dict = Depends(verify_token)` as a parameter to every route handler function. Add `organizationId` scoping to all MongoDB queries.
fixEvidence: CWE-287 / OWASP A01 — ai_policy_generator_python/app/api/routes/ — no verify_token dependency on any handler
